I've just opened PR #36677, which bridges Partrec.rfind with total unbounded search (Nat.find).

Specifically, it adds two missing pieces to Computability.Partrec:

  • Computable.find: Proves that x ↦ Nat.find (h_ex x) is computable for a computable decidable predicate P.

  • Computable.rightInverse_of_surjective: Proves that the right inverse of a computable surjective function is computable.

All CI checks are green. I would greatly appreciate it if someone could take a look or bump it into the review queue.

My PR #36677 is failing CI with error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date right after I merged master.

It builds fine locally, and I didn't touch the manifest or toolchain. I see other recent PRs (like #37534) are green — could this be a missing cache issue specific to forks?

I took a look at your PR and the latest merge of master seems to be commit 617fab9, whose parents are a64c277 and 41280ad.

The former is from your branch and the latter is a commit from master from 2 weeks ago. Judging from the commit message of 617fab9, which reads "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into partrec-nat-find", maybe instead of origin/master (which could be outdated, as the origin remote presumably points to your fork), you want to merge upstream/master instead?

git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/master

I'm assuming you followed the instructions here to set up your git remotes.

If so then updating your local master branch first and then merging that into your PR branch might be a good alternative approach:

git switch master
git pull
git switch partrec-nat-find
git merge master

These steps update your local master so that new branches created off of it will also be up to date.
@Bryan Gin-ge Chen Thank you!
